admission-controller.md.title: Admission Controller
admission-controller.md.summary: This document describes the Admission Controller, a code component that intercepts Kubernetes API requests before they are persisted. It explains that controllers can be validating or mutating, and that any controller can reject requests.

admission-policies.md.title: Explore Validating and Mutating Admission Policies
admission-policies.md.summary: This document explains declarative admission policies using Common Expression Language (CEL) in Kubernetes, detailing how ValidatingAdmissionPolicy enforces constraints and MutatingAdmissionPolicy modifies resources. It covers policy elements, CEL expressions, parameter resources, and the difference between validating and mutating modes.

affinity.md.title: Kubernetes Scheduling and Affinity
affinity.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes affinity rules that guide scheduler placement of pods, covering node and pod-to-pod affinity types based on labels and selectors.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Aggregation Layer
aggregation-layer.md.summary: This document explains how to install additional Kubernetes-style APIs in a cluster by configuring the API Server to support additional APIs and adding APIService objects to claim URL paths.

annotation.md.title: Annotation
annotation.md.summary: This document defines annotations as key-value pairs used to attach non-identifying metadata to objects, explaining their flexibility in size, structure, and content while noting that clients can retrieve this data.

api-group.md.title: API Group
api-group.md.summary: This document explains how to manage Kubernetes API groups, enabling/disabling them via server configuration and defining paths for specific resources.

api-resource.md.title: Kubernetes API Resource
api-resource.md.summary: This document defines the Kubernetes API resource type, explaining that it is an endpoint on the Kubernetes API server representing an HTTP request to an object or operation.

app-container.md.title: App Container Documentation
app-container.md.summary: This document defines app containers as pods that run after init containers finish, allowing separation of initialization details from application logic.

application-architect.md.title: Application Architect
application-architect.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Application Architect, who designs high-level app structures to ensure scalability and maintainability by interacting with surrounding components like databases and microservices.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Application Security Checklist
application-security-checklist.md.summary: This document outlines a developer's guide to securing Kubernetes applications, covering base hardening, service account management, pod-level and container-level security contexts, RBAC, image security, and network policies.

approver.md.title: Approver
approver.md.summary: A role for Kubernetes contributors to review and approve code contributions, focusing on holistic acceptance rather than just code quality.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture
architecture.md.summary: This document outlines the components required for a complete Kubernetes cluster, including the control plane (kube-apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager) and worker nodes (kubelet, kube-proxy, cloud-controller-manager). It details how nodes host Pods, manages services, and handles events, while noting that kube-proxy is optional depending on network plugins.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Hardening Guide - Authentication Mechanisms
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: This guide explains Kubernetes' built-in authentication mechanisms including X.509 client certificates, static token files, and bootstrap tokens. It warns against using these for production clusters due to certificate revocation risks, lack of permanent records, and password-protected keys that expose secrets.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes Authorization Guide
authorization.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes API requests are evaluated for access control, detailing authorization verdicts, request attributes, and modes. It clarifies that requests must pass through admission controllers, with deny decisions made after authorization modules complete their checks.

autoscaling.md.title: Autoscaling Workloads
autoscaling.md.summary: This document explains how to scale Kubernetes workloads manually (horizontal/vertical) and automatically using HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) and VerticalPodAutoscaler (VPA) based on cluster size or schedules.

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor
cadvisor.md.summary: cAdvisor is a daemon that monitors and exports resource usage (CPU, memory, network) and performance metrics for running containers.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI) Specification
cdi.md.summary: CDI defines how Kubernetes workloads configure devices like bind mounts and environment variables within containers using device plugins and dynamic resource allocation.

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language
cel.md.summary: This document describes CEL, a general-purpose expression language designed for fast, portable, and safe execution in Kubernetes. It enables fine-grained filtering using dynamic admission controllers and resource allocation via dynamic resource allocation.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes Certificate
certificate.md.summary: This document explains the purpose of certificates in Kubernetes, which are cryptographically secure files used to validate access to the cluster API.

cgroup.md.title: cgroup (control group)
cgroup.md.summary: This document explains cgroup, a Linux kernel feature that limits, accounts for, and isolates resource usage like CPU, memory, and disk I/O for a collection of processes.

cidr.md.title: CIDR
cidr.md.summary: CIDR is a notation for describing blocks of IP addresses used in networking and Kubernetes node configuration.

cla.md.title: CLA (Contributor License Agreement)
cla.md.summary: This document outlines the terms under which contributors grant licenses to open source projects for their work, helping resolve legal disputes regarding intellectual property.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: A Kubernetes component that decouples cloud infrastructure from cluster logic, allowing cloud providers to release features at different speeds than the main Kubernetes project.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Cloud Native Security and Kubernetes
cloud-native-security.md.summary: This document outlines the lifecycle phases for securing cloud-native platforms, including development, distribution, and deployment. It details security controls for each phase, such as zero trust architecture, supply chain security for container images, and runtime protection for compute and storage resources.

cloud-provider.md.title: Cloud Provider
cloud-provider.md.summary: This document defines a cloud provider as a business offering cloud computing platforms, including managed infrastructure like IaaS and Kubernetes as PaaS.

cluster-administration.md.title: Cluster Administration Guide
cluster-administration.md.summary: This guide covers planning, managing, and securing Kubernetes clusters, including node management, resource quotas, and security features like certificates and admission controllers.

cluster-operations.md.title: Cluster Operations
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document outlines the work involved in managing a Kubernetes cluster, including day-to-day operations, co-ordinating upgrades, and responding to events.

cluster-operator.md.title: Cluster Operator
cluster-operator.md.summary: A person who configures, controls, and monitors clusters, responsible for keeping them up and running with periodic maintenance or upgrades.

cluster.md.title: Cluster
cluster.md.summary: This document defines a cluster as a set of worker nodes running containerized applications, where the control plane manages the nodes and Pods for fault-tolerant high availability.

cncf.md.title: CNCF Documentation
cncf.md.summary: The CNCF is a sub-foundation of the Linux Foundation focused on building sustainable ecosystems and fostering a community around projects that orchestrate containers within microservices architectures.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI) Documentation
cni.md.summary: This document explains CNI plugins, which are Network plugins adhering to the appc/CNI specification. It references the Network Plugins section for Kubernetes-specific details.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Components
components.md.summary: This document outlines the essential components of a Kubernetes cluster, including the control plane (apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager) and worker nodes (kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime), along with optional addons like DNS and Web UI.

condition.md.title: Kubernetes Condition Documentation
condition.md.summary: This document defines Kubernetes conditions, which are fields in resource status that describe the current state of a Kubernetes component. It explains how conditions use a type, status, reason, and message fields to communicate resource status.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Guide
configuration.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes separates configuration from code, detailing ConfigMaps, Secrets, and helper containers (sidecar/init) for managing cluster and pod-level settings securely.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: This document defines container environment variables as name=value pairs essential for containerized applications, detailing their role in providing cluster resources like service endpoints alongside application details.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime
container-runtime.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes' container runtime interface, detailing supported runtimes like containerd and cri-o, and their role in managing container execution within the Kubernetes environment.

container.md.title: Container
container.md.summary: This document defines containers as lightweight, portable executable images containing software and dependencies, which decouple applications from host infrastructure for easier deployment and scaling.

containerd.md.title: containerd
containerd.md.summary: containerd is a lightweight container runtime that manages images, executes containers, and provides network access on Linux and Windows.

containers.md.title: Containers
containers.md.summary: This document explains containers, their images, and runtimes, detailing how they decouple applications from host infrastructure, how they are stateless and immutable, and how to manage different container runtimes in Kubernetes clusters.

contributor.md.title: Contributor
contributor.md.summary: This document defines a Contributor as someone who donates code, documentation, or time to help the Kubernetes project or community, including PRs, issues, and SIG participation.

control-plane.md.title: Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: This document describes the container orchestration layer that manages container lifecycles via API, composed of components like etcd, API Server, Scheduler, and Controller Manager.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum CPU Constraints for a Namespace
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to set Kubernetes limits on CPU resources for containers and Pods within a namespace. It details the process of creating a LimitRange with specific min/max CPU values, verifying pod compliance, and enforcing these constraints to prevent resource exhaustion.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default CPU Requests and Limits for a Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This guide explains how to create namespaces, define LimitRanges and Pods with default CPU limits and requests, and demonstrates scenarios where containers specify limits without requests.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a Kubernetes tool enabling OCI-compliant container runtimes and remote image fetching.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob Documentation
cron-jobs.md.summary: This document explains how to create, write, and manage CronJob jobs using YAML spec syntax. It details the Cron format, schedule syntax, Vixie cron steps, concurrency policies, and job history limits.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI) Guide
csi.md.summary: This document explains how to use the Container Storage Interface (CSI) to expose storage systems to containers, enabling out-of-tree plugins for Kubernetes without adding them to the repository.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: This document explains how to use CustomResourceDefinitions to extend Kubernetes APIs without building a full server, allowing environments to add custom resources if built-in ones are insufficient.

daemonset.md.title: DaemonSet Documentation
daemonset.md.summary: This document explains how to create, manage, and deploy DaemonSets in Kubernetes, detailing their purpose for running cluster-wide services like storage or monitoring, required fields, pod templates, and scheduling rules.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This document provides resources for fixing issues with containerized applications, covering common Kubernetes resource problems, container termination messages, and debugging techniques.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Clusters
debug-cluster.md.summary: This guide provides step-by-step methods to diagnose and resolve cluster issues, including checking node registration, debugging down/unreachable nodes via kubectl commands, and analyzing logs to identify root causes.

deployment.md.title: Kubernetes Deployments
deployment.md.summary: This document outlines the deployment lifecycle and configuration for Kubernetes, including use cases, creating deployments with specific replicas and selectors, rolling updates, and rollback strategies.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin
device-plugin.md.summary: Device plugins allow pods to access hardware resources on specific nodes by advertising them to the kubelet, enabling vendor-specific initialization.

device-plugins.md.title: Device Plugins
device-plugins.md.summary: This document describes Kubernetes device plugins, which allow vendors to advertise hardware resources (like GPUs) to kubelets. It details registration via gRPC, scheduling constraints, and deployment methods, while also covering implementation steps and API endpoints.

device.md.title: Device Documentation
device.md.summary: This document defines devices as infrastructure resources attached to nodes, including commercial products like GPUs and custom hardware like ASIC boards, which require device drivers for Kubernetes Pods to access.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass Documentation
deviceclass.md.summary: This document explains how administrators define DeviceClasses to claim and utilize dynamic resource allocation (DRA) within a cluster.

disruption.md.title: Disruption
disruption.md.summary: This document defines disruptions as events causing Pods to go out of service, distinguishing between voluntary (e.g., node failure) and involuntary (e.g., outage) scenarios, and links to the Kubernetes documentation for further details.

dns-pod-service.md.title: Kubernetes DNS for Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes creates DNS records for Services and Pods, detailing A/AAAA records, SRV records, and how pod namespaces affect query resolution.

docker.md.title: Docker
docker.md.summary: Docker Engine provides OS-level virtualization using Linux kernel features like cgroups and namespaces to isolate containers within a single Linux instance, avoiding VM overhead.

dockershim.md.title: Dockershim
dockershim.md.summary: Dockershim is a Kubernetes component that enables kubelets to communicate with Docker Engine, but it was removed starting with version 1.24.

downstream.md.title: Downstream (disambiguation)
downstream.md.summary: This document explains the technical distinction between 'downstream' and 'upstream' in the Kubernetes ecosystem, where downstream refers to code or tools relying on the core Kubernetes codebase, while upstream refers to the original source repository.

downward-api.md.title: Downward API
downward-api.md.summary: This document explains the Downward API, a mechanism allowing containers to access Kubernetes metadata (name, namespace, labels, annotations) and pod-level fields (service account, node name) without using Kubernetes client APIs. It details how to use `fieldRef` for environment variables and `resourceFieldRef` for volume-based access to these fields.

drain.md.title: kubectl drain command
drain.md.summary: The `kubectl drain` command marks a Node as going out of service by evicting all Pods from it, allowing for maintenance or removal. It retries rejected requests until pods are terminated or a timeout occurs.

dual-stack.md.title: IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking
dual-stack.md.summary: This document explains IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking, which enables Kubernetes clusters to assign both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses to Pods and Services. It details prerequisites like Kubernetes 1.20+, provider support, and specific configuration steps for kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-proxy, and kubelet to enable this feature.

duration.md.title: Duration in Kubernetes
duration.md.summary: This document explains how to represent time durations in Kubernetes, specifically using Go's time.Duration type with units like ns, µs, ms, s, m, and h.

dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.title: Dynamic Volume Provisioning
dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.summary: This document describes how users can request automatic creation of storage volumes via an API, eliminating the need for cluster administrators to pre-provision storage.

endpoint-slice.md.title: EndpointSlice Documentation
endpoint-slice.md.summary: EndpointSlices track backend IP addresses for Kubernetes Services, typically backing Pods. The control plane manages them automatically, but manual definition is possible for Services without selectors.

endpoint-slices.md.title: EndpointSlices API
endpoint-slices.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes EndpointSlices manage network endpoints for services, defining address types (IPv4/IPv6), serving/terminating/ready conditions, and managing up to 1000 endpoints per slice.

endpoint.md.title: Endpoints API
endpoint.md.summary: Deprecated Kubernetes API that replaced EndpointsSlices since v1.21, explaining its deprecation due to scalability concerns.

ephemeral-container.md.title: Ephemeral Container
ephemeral-container.md.summary: Ephemeral containers are temporary pods used for diagnostic purposes within a pod, lacking resource guarantees and not suitable for running workload components.

etcd.md.title: etcd
etcd.md.summary: etcd is a consistent and highly-available key-value store used as Kubernetes' backing store for cluster data. It requires a backup plan for data if the cluster uses it.

event.md.title: Kubernetes Event Documentation
event.md.summary: This document explains what Kubernetes events are, their purpose for tracking state changes and triggers, and emphasizes that they should be treated as informative data rather than authoritative records.

eviction.md.title: Eviction
eviction.md.summary: Eviction is the process of terminating Pods on Nodes, covering two types: Node-pressure eviction and API-initiated eviction.

extensions.md.title: Extensions
extensions.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes extensions allow administrators to deploy and use pre-installed cluster software, reducing the need for manual installation and enabling new hardware types.

feature-gates.md.title: Feature Gate Documentation
feature-gates.md.summary: This document explains feature gates as opaque keys used to control which Kubernetes features are enabled in a cluster, allowing components to selectively activate or deactivate specific features.

finalizer.md.title: Kubernetes Finalizer
finalizer.md.summary: Kubernetes uses finalizers to wait for specific cleanup conditions before deleting resources marked for deletion, allowing control over garbage collection.

flexvolume.md.title: FlexVolume
flexvolume.md.summary: FlexVolume is a deprecated Kubernetes volume plugin interface that requires root access for driver installation. It is being replaced by the Container Storage Interface (CSI) to address limitations.

gateway.md.title: Gateway API
gateway.md.summary: Gateway API is an extensible, role-oriented configuration mechanism for dynamic infrastructure provisioning in Kubernetes, defined by four stable API kinds: GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, and GRPCRoute.

glossary-api-eviction.md.title: API-initiated eviction
glossary-api-eviction.md.summary: This document explains how to use the Kubernetes API to create an Eviction object that triggers graceful pod termination via the kube-apiserver, respecting PodDisruptionBudgets and terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

glossary-configmap.md.title: ConfigMap
glossary-configmap.md.summary: ConfigMap is an API object used to store non-confidential data in key-value pairs, allowing pods to consume environment variables, command-line arguments, or configuration files in volume.

glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This document explains how containers use PostStart and PreStop hooks to execute code immediately after creation and before termination.

glossary-controller.md.title: Kubernetes Controller Documentation
glossary-controller.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes controllers function as control loops that monitor cluster state and make changes to achieve desired configurations, running within the control plane.

glossary-cri.md.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI) Protocol
glossary-cri.md.summary: CRI defines the gRPC protocol used by kubelet to communicate with the container runtime, enabling efficient inter-component communication.

glossary-deployment.md.title: Deployment
glossary-deployment.md.summary: This document explains how to deploy a replicated application using Pods, which are distributed across cluster nodes. It also notes that StatefulSets are recommended for workloads requiring local state.

glossary-downward-api.md.title: Downward API
glossary-downward-api.md.summary: Kubernetes mechanism to expose Pod and container field values to code running in a container, allowing applications to access cluster information without modifying their own code.

glossary-dra.md.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation
glossary-dra.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes' Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) feature, which allows cluster admins to define device classes and claim hardware accelerators for workloads. It details how Kubernetes allocates matching devices to specific Pods on nodes capable of accessing those devices.

glossary-garbage-collection.md.title: Kubernetes Garbage Collection
glossary-garbage-collection.md.summary: Kubernetes uses garbage collection to clean up cluster resources like unused containers, failed pods, and expired objects.

glossary-kube-scheduler.md.title: kube-scheduler
glossary-kube-scheduler.md.summary: The kube-scheduler is a control plane component that selects nodes for newly created Pods to run on, considering resource requirements, hardware constraints, and data locality.

glossary-kubectl.md.title: Kubectl
glossary-kubectl.md.summary: Kubectl is a command-line tool for communicating with a Kubernetes cluster's control plane using the Kubernetes API.

glossary-kubernetes-api.md.title: Kubernetes API
glossary-kubernetes-api.md.summary: This document describes the HTTP API used by Kubernetes to communicate with cluster components and external systems, allowing users to query and manipulate Kubernetes objects via RESTful calls.

glossary-logging.md.title: Logging
glossary-logging.md.summary: This document explains how logs are generated by cluster and applications, detailing their purpose for debugging and monitoring cluster activity.

glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.title: Mixed Version Proxy (MVP) Feature
glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.summary: This document explains the Mixed Version Proxy (MVP) feature in Kubernetes, which allows kube-apiservers to proxy resource requests to different API servers based on their version compatibility.

glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.title: Node-pressure eviction
glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.summary: This document explains how the kubelet proactively terminates pods to reclaim resources on nodes when CPU, memory, or disk space reaches specific consumption levels, preventing starvation.

glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.title: Pod Lifecycle
glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.summary: This document defines the five phases of a Pod's life: Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, and Unknown. It explains that the `phase` field in PodStatus represents the current state of the pod.

glossary-pod-security-policy.md.title: Pod Security Policy
glossary-pod-security-policy.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes Pod Security Policies, which enforce security restrictions during pod creation and updates. It notes that the policy was deprecated in v1.21 and removed in v1.25, recommending Pod Security Admission or third-party plugins as alternatives.

glossary-secret.md.title: Secrets
glossary-secret.md.summary: This document explains how to store sensitive data like passwords and OAuth tokens securely using base64 encoded values, with options to encrypt them at rest. It details how pods can reference secrets via volume mounts or environment variables, distinguishing between confidential data (Secrets) and non-confidential data (ConfigMaps).

glossary-security-context.md.title: Security Context
glossary-security-context.md.summary: This document explains how to configure privilege and access control settings for Pods and containers, including user, group, and SELinux/AppArmor/Seccomp policies.
